items.title: Hy4 by Tencent is FULLY FREE & Crazy!
items.summary:
Sponsored by WorkBuddy. Check them out here: https://www.workbuddy.ai/?fromSource=gwzcw.24559268.24559268.24559268&utm_medium=cpm&utm_id=gwzcw.24559268.24559268.24559268

In this video, I'll look at Tencent Hy4, the first Hy model with vision, which launched on November 4th, along with Tencent's claims and the caveats that come with them. I'll explain the difference between Hy4, the model, and WorkBuddy, Tencent's desktop agent app, and show how to set it up and pick Hy4 in the model picker. Then I'll run two demos: a sales dashboard with a planted mistake that Hy4 has to catch, and a task board screenshot that it has to rebuild as a working web page. After that, I'll cover how I would test it, the API pricing and the free window inside WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy, and give my verdict.

--
Key Takeaways:

🚀 Hy4 is the official release from Tencent Hy, launched on November 4th, and it is the first Hy model that can read charts, screenshots and documents.
⚠️ Tencent says it ranks amo
items.author: AICodeKing
items.transcript: [music] >> Hi, welcome to another video. Tencent Hi, that's spelled h y and pronounced Hi, has released Hi 4. And this is the official Hi 4, not a preview build. It launched on November 4th and the big change is that Hi 4 can see. It's the first Hi model with vision, so it can read charts, screenshots, and documents. And Tencent says it can also use a computer in the terminal and in normal desktop apps. Tencent says it now ranks among the leading open models, but they also say it still trails the top closed models and the weights weren't out at launch. So take the claims with a grain of salt and let's actually use it. Now, one thing that confuses people. Hi 4 is the model, the part that reads your input and writes the answer. Work buddy is Tencent's desktop agent app, the part that plans the steps, opens your files, and hands you a finished result. So Hi 4 does the thinking, work buddy does the work. And you can switch the model inside work buddy without changing anything else. Setting it up is simple. Download work buddy from workbuddy.ai for Mac or Windows, install it, and log in. Then open the model picker at the bottom right of the input box and choose Hi 4. You can paste a screenshot with command v or click the plus button to attach files and type your task and send it. So let's do the first demo. I made a small sales dashboard for a fictional shop, a short commentary about it with a mistake planet in it, and the raw numbers as a CSV file, so I know the right answer. I'm attaching all three and asking Hi 4 to find what doesn't match, redo the September to October math, and write a corrected one-page note for leadership. Now, I don't just trust the answer. The right answer is that revenue went up 20% because orders went up 20%, while the average order value stayed flat at $50. So average spend per order didn't rise and the numbers can't tell us why orders grew. Hi 4 caught that wrong explanation. It took about 12 minutes on that one prompt and it fixed its own page layout along the way. Let's put the dashboard and Hi 4's notes side by side and check each number. The second demo is more visual. I made a screenshot of a simple task board with three columns to do in progress and done and switched work buddy to coding mode. The prompt asks Hi 4 to rebuild it as a single working web page that lets me add tasks, move them between columns, search them, and keeps everything after a reload. Then I open what it built next to the original screenshot and actually test it. To be fair, it needed one round of feedback from me to fix two bugs, so this isn't a first try. Now I add a task, move it, search for it, and reload the page because a board that looks right but forgets everything isn't really a task board. With those fixes, it passes all of these checks. After it delivered, it kept doing extra work, so I stopped it, and that's why Work Buddy shows this run as canceled. Now I ran three more tests that a vision model should handle, a folder of receipts, a pencil sketch, and a photo of a printed report. The first one is a desk task. Work Buddy doesn't have a tool for clicking around the desktop, so this is file work in a folder. I gave it an inbox with seven files, receipt photos, PDFs and email receipt, a CSV, and a personal note. I asked it to keep only the real October expenses, fill a spreadsheet, and export a one-page report. Hi Four opened every file and finished in about seven minutes. The total it reported is $462.23. That's $51.90 for meals, $64.18 for supplies, $318.75 for printing, and $27.40 for travel, and that matches my answer key. It left three files out, a September taxi receipt, a quote that isn't an invoice, and a shopping list with a reason for each. The second one starts from a pencil sketch of a striped lighthouse, a cottage, and a sailing boat with a few handwritten notes. I attached it in coding mode and asked for a single-file 3D scene in Three.js. It took about nine minutes and came back with one HTML file I can drag to look around. The beam spins, clicking the lamp switches the light on and off, and the boat bobs on the waves. So it read the handwritten notes, not only the drawing. The third one is a photo of a one-page energy report with seven questions. The catch is note three. The gym's August reading includes 1,800 kilowatt-hours that isn't real use, so the chart makes August look biggest. Hi Four answered in under two minutes, and it applied the note. The gym's August is 3,090. The Q3 total drops from 37,580 to 35,780, and September becomes the highest month. Main Hall used the most in September, 3,960. The library went up 12.2%. The estimated cost is $5,335 and 76 cents, and the workshop uses the most per square meter. With corrections due by November 15th, all seven answers match my key. That's how I would test it, too. Use your own files, keep the same prompt and settings, and change only the model if you're comparing. Also, image input means it reads images, it doesn't generate them. As for pricing, the API is about 83 cents per million input tokens and about $2.50 per million output tokens, the same as Hi4 Preview, and 10 cent Cloud Token Hub bills it at half price through December 31st. It caught a wrong explanation in a sales report on its own and built a working board after one round of feedback. So if your work is full of charts and screenshots, the vision side is what I'd try first. Overall, it's pretty cool. Anyway, let me know your thoughts in the comments. If you like this video, consider donating through the Super Thanks option or becoming a member by clicking the join button. Also, give this video a thumbs [music] up and subscribe to my channel. I'll see you in the next one. Until then, bye.
